gates.name: workflow-harness
gates.when: a methodFiles entry or a file under .claude/rules/ changed

board.vocabulary: Module vocabulary: dense item ids in BoardStore with idOfKey/keyOfId (there are no nids and no onCapacityGrew; per-id arrays grow in lockstep in the store), TWO coordinate spaces (content and viewport-paint, plus track space for spans), the animation sources under BoardAnimationCoordinator (TrackResizeAnimator, ItemEnterExitAnimator, ItemSlideEngine, MakeRoomEngine), obtain-to-retain retention, OverlapLaneResolver lanes, the BoardDragController drag layer with BoardDropResolver, and BoardAnimationStyle families with a per-family kill switch: a family whose resolved duration is not positive is off.

lensAddenda.correctness: Degradation also includes an item mid-exit and an unlaid or detached port.
lensAddenda.performance: Hot paths that hash keys instead of using the id-keyed reads.
lensAddenda.interaction: A plan silent on what happens when its change coincides with a bulk animation, a drag's make-room preview, an exiting item held by retention or a frozen track has not covered it.

sliver_tree.vocabulary: Module vocabulary: nids and the *Nid hot-path variants, three coordinate spaces (sliver scroll, sliver paint, viewport scroll), five animation sources under AnimationCoordinator, exit and edge ghosts, sticky pins, pending-deletion nodes, TreeAnimationStyle families with a per-family zero kill switch.

lensAddenda.correctness: Degradation also includes a defunct scrollable and a pending-deletion node.
lensAddenda.performance: Hot paths that hash keys instead of using the *Nid method variants.
lensAddenda.interaction: A plan silent on what happens when its change coincides with a bulk animation, a reorder preview, an exit ghost or a sticky pin has not covered it.

correctness.addendum: In this codebase re-entrancy includes anything that can abort and re-run a layout, plus frame ordering and settle transitions. Teardown includes dispose, ticker cancellation and recognizer disposal. Degradation includes an animation family switched off (a kill switch that dominates explicit per-call durations), hot reload, and a mutation issued mid-animation, mid-drag or inside a batch. Lifecycle includes what the framework does without the feature's code running: a build that throws, after which the element shows an ErrorWidget and its next build creates new children; a kept-alive child dropped from its sliver and adopted back without a rebuild; and a GlobalKey moving a subtree, whose render objects are detached and attached under the new parent.

performance.addendum: Per-frame allocation. Debug counters pin performance contracts here, so a plan names the counter and its expected value.

interaction.addendum: Here the crossings are every animation source, paint pass, mutator, widget layer and entry point.

timing.addendum: Here: a settle transition whose notify order is described but not asserted, a scroll correction whose re-entrancy is reasoned about but not exercised, a tick whose paint-only or layout-triggering status is claimed but not pinned by a debug counter. Running a frame is the test.

planRules: Every geometric value the plan introduces is tagged with its coordinate space, as the module's architecture rules name the spaces.
An animation the plan installs declares its style family once, at the site that resolves its spec; nothing downstream re-derives it.
Every public symbol states whether the barrel exports it: the package exports through explicit show clauses, so an undeclared export is unnameable by app code.
New per-id storage names its growth path and the sites that clear it on release.
A new debug counter or @visibleForTesting member is a test seam: the Testing Plan names the existing seam it rejected and why.
